summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C cirrhosis and portal hypertension, was admitted for melena and hematemesis following recent esophageal variceal banding. He presented with hypotension and evidence of upper GI bleeding, requiring transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. An EGD revealed an esophageal ulcer and blood in the stomach, but no active bleeding; the previously placed variceal bands had dislodged. He was treated with octreotide, ceftriaxone (later switched to oral ciprofloxacin), and IV pantoprazole, which was transitioned to oral pantoprazole twice daily. Nadolol was held due to bradycardia, likely related to octreotide, but was restarted at discharge at half dose. His condition stabilized, hemoglobin remained steady, and he tolerated a diet advance. He was discharged home with instructions to complete a course of ciprofloxacin and sucralfate, continue high-dose PPI therapy, and follow up for repeat EGD and hepatology evaluation.
